source.title: Landscape Connectivity and Dropout Stability of SGD Solutions for Over-parameterized Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including supplementary material, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures how post-training neuron removal affects population risk and classification error as network width changes. It does not test the specific interventions or measures in V1–V8.
record.gate_note: The experiments remove half the neurons from trained networks and report resulting population risk or classification error. The paper also reports path-connectivity experiments, but those measure loss along parameter paths rather than the claim versions' outcomes. Figure values without accompanying textual numbers are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The study tests post-training neuron-removal stability and connectivity between SGD solutions, neither of which is a claim version here. Increasing width reduces removal-induced degradation, but the study does not establish that test error keeps falling beyond the width needed for zero training error (V2). Post-training removal does not test dropout during training (V6), and path connectivity does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps (V7).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors prove increasingly strong dropout stability and approximate connectivity of SGD solutions as width grows, and validate these phenomena numerically. The guarantees concern the stated mean-field, online-SGD assumptions; multilayer theory fixes the first and last layers, while the classification experiments train all layers.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies post-training neuron removal with rescaling and connectivity of SGD solutions; it does not test the claim versions' training interventions or measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported removal-related classification-error increase varies across dataset and architecture; the plotted degradation decreases as width grows.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing half the hidden neurons with rescaling causes progressively smaller performance degradation as width increases. At width 12800, reported error increases range from 0.35 to 3.6 percentage points across the four architecture–dataset settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD-trained networks become increasingly stable to fixed post-training neuron removal as width increases.

fits_no_version.finding: Theoretical bounds and numerical experiments connect different SGD solutions through piecewise linear paths with small loss barriers; the theoretical barriers vanish with width under the stated assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Overparameterization and SGD yield approximately connected solutions through dropout stability.

record.problems: Numerical experiments use 20 independent trials; results for most widths are shown only in figures. The experiments use VGG-16 features for CIFAR-10 in the main setup; the text says direct fully connected training on CIFAR-10 gives qualitatively similar results with larger classification error, without giving numbers.
record.rows_left_out: Figure-only values across other widths, intermediate training times, and the path-connectivity experiments were not extracted because the text provides no additional assignable numerical outcomes for the selected result rows.

untested.parts: Fitting fixed random labels alongside natural-label generalization and chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Test-error trends beyond an identified zero-training-error width threshold. Removal-induced degradation versus width does not establish this trend.
Controlled comparisons of convolutional and fully connected networks trained from scratch, including the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover held-out performance.
The effect of adding dropout during training on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, its association with train–test gaps, and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The numerical results use test-set averages and 20 independent trials. They concern stability after neuron removal, not improved generalization from training with dropout. The synthetic Gaussian task has informative class-conditional inputs and does not constitute a fixed-random-label experiment.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the role of local connectivity.
Large-batch versus small-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout used during training and its effect on test error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with the train–test gap.
Removing influential memorized training examples and its effect on test accuracy.
